results.title: FSSAI tightens pan masala packaging norms, specifies plastic-free materials
results.description: New Delhi: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has tightened packaging norms for pan masala by specifying materials that can be used for its packaging. Under the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, paper, paperboard, cellulose and other naturally derived materials can be used for pan masala packaging only if they are free from plastic. The notification specifically mentions polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and other synthetic polymers or copolymers. The packaging must also be free from laminates, aluminium foil and metallised layers. Tin and glass containers have also been specified as packaging options for pan masala. The amendment adds pan masala to Schedule IV of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018, which contains the list of suggested packaging materials. FSSAI also said provisions under clauses (f) and (i) of Rule 4(1) of the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, as amended, will apply to pan masala packaging. The regulations will come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. FSSAI had issued a draft of the amendment on April 28, 2026, inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders. The regulator said the responses received were considered before finalising the regulations. The final notification was issued on August 7, 2026, by FSSAI Chief Executive Officer Rajit Punhani.
